sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
319. (1) A person is said to cheat by personation if he cheats by pretending to be some other person, or by knowingly substituting one person for or another, or representing that he or any other person is a person other than he or such other person really is
(2) Whoever cheats by personation shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both

(b) A cheats by pretending to be B, a person who is deceased. A cheats by personation

sections.heading: Explanations
sections.body: Explanation.—The offence is committed whether the individual personated is a real or imaginary person

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 319 constitutes a key component of Chapter XVII (Of Offences against Property) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing cheating by personation. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of cheating by personation under Section 319 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 319.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 319 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 319 vs General Attempt: Section 319 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XVII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.
Section 319 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 319 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences against Property.

Rule: Under BNS s. 319, liability attaches upon proof of the statutory actus reus accompanied by the requisite mens rea without lawful justification.
Application: The evidence demonstrates that the accused performed the specified act with the required state of mind, satisfying all statutory ingredients of Section 319.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 319 and subject to the prescribed punishment.
